about: The Looks the New video picker offers. Add, remove or hide one by editing this file; the editor reads it through bridge/looks.py, so no editor build is needed. Paths are relative to this folder. Only entries with approved: true are shown.

picker.library_styles_note: Converted library Looks are offered for new videos only when approved; the rest are hidden from new selections. Existing projects can still read their recipes and defaults by Look id.

styles.label: Talking head
styles.line: One person talking to the camera: cut well, with the flavour you pick next.

styles.label: Made with code
styles.line: No footage needed: your AI writes and draws the whole video.

looks.label: Hands at work
looks.line: Real hands, changing material, and an honest stopping point.
looks.needs: The same object or material before, during and after a visible change.

asks.label: What should the viewer understand?
asks.hint: The task, change or function; include verified claims or limits.

looks.label: Clean
looks.line: Just you, cut well: calm captions, gentle punch-ins, clear sound.
looks.needs: Any talking head with steady framing and enough resolution to punch in a little. A good speaker carries it.

looks.label: Big Letters Behind You
looks.line: On key words the room drops away and a huge word lands behind your head.
looks.needs: A steady talking head with headroom above the head, in a place with a few clear colors. Needs the person cut out (the cut-out model runs on this PC).

looks.label: Scenes Behind You
looks.line: The wall opens and a drawn world plays out behind you, timed to your words.
looks.needs: A steady talking head who stays roughly in place, with a clean outline against the room. Needs the person cut out; the first time takes a while per second of video.

looks.label: You + Visuals On Top
looks.line: You sit low; a panel above draws what you are saying as you say it.
looks.needs: A steady talking head with headroom, saying things with a shape: lists, processes, comparisons, a problem and its answer. A purely emotional story has nothing to draw.

looks.label: Big words with mood cutaways
looks.line: You talk to the camera while your key words pop up big, and short moody clips of what you mean cut in between.
looks.needs: One person talking to the camera with clear speech about something they feel. Filmed cutaways come from licensed stock or their own filming.

looks.label: Filmed scrapbook
looks.line: One camera move over a scrapbook page, your pictures taped on it, a voice telling the story.
looks.needs: A description, and 4 to 8 sharp pictures that each show one clear thing. It says only what you tell it and what the pictures show.

asks.label: What's it about?
asks.hint: Tell the story with the facts in it. It won't add any you don't give.

asks.label: Pictures to show
asks.hint: These go on the page. 4 to 8, each showing one clear thing.
asks.instead: your AI draws the pictures itself, which looks plainer

asks.label: What it should look like
asks.hint: For the feel only: these never appear in the video.

asks.label: Your voiceover
asks.hint: A recording of yours. Empty: your AI writes the script and a voice on this PC reads it.

looks.label: Flat Explainer
looks.line: Name a topic: illustrated places and people act it out while a voice explains.
looks.needs: A topic with places and actions in it: why something happens, how it works, a what-if, a true story. It states only facts it can support.

asks.label: What should it explain?
asks.hint: A sentence is enough. Add any facts you want used: it won't state what it can't support.

asks.label: Your voiceover
asks.hint: A recording of yours. Empty: your AI writes the script and a voice on this PC reads it.

looks.label: Drawn Story
looks.line: Tell a story: your AI draws it as a comic or storybook that comes alive.
looks.needs: A story, from one line up: who it's about, what happens, how it ends. A true story is told only from what you say.

asks.label: What's the story?
asks.hint: Who it's about, what happens, how it ends. Say if it really happened: it won't add to a true story.

asks.label: Your voiceover
asks.hint: A recording of yours. Empty: your AI writes the script and a voice on this PC reads it.

looks.label: Orbit Stack
looks.line: A commercial for your software: you talk, and cards of it in use float around you.
looks.needs: A steady talking head about the software, with a clean outline, and a recording of it in use. Needs the person cut out; the first time takes a while per second of video.

asks.label: Your software in use
asks.hint: A screen recording, 15 to 60 seconds of what you talk about. Only what's in it gets shown. Screenshots or a logo can go here too.

asks.label: Its name, spelled right
asks.hint: And anything else it should get right. It claims only what you say, write here or show.

looks.label: Flat vector
looks.line: Crisp flat shapes, long shadows and a soft grain: your idea as an editorial illustration.
looks.needs: A story or an idea, from one line up: your AI writes the script and draws the whole video. It adds nothing to a true story.

looks.label: One place, one moment
looks.line: Recognise the place, watch the event, leave on its natural release. Passed re-review after checker fixes.
looks.needs: One coherent place, an observable action and natural ending; real location sound.

looks.label: Performance first
looks.line: The actor leads the cut; light and framing serve the dramatic beat.
looks.needs: A scripted exchange with matching coverage and usable production dialogue.

looks.label: The journey
looks.line: Arrive, explore, leave; the place has a voice between the music.

looks.label: Highlight reel
looks.line: Anticipation, atmosphere, the peak, and its release.

looks.label: Before and after
looks.line: Separate Webb assemblies become a telescope element through precision work, lifting and joining.

looks.label: Trailer
looks.line: Newlyweds build a kit house; construction turns into escalating physical comedy, with the ending withheld.

looks.label: Archive story
looks.line: Apollo 11 through archive pictures and original mission voices.
looks.needs: Apollo 11 through archive pictures and original mission voices.

looks.label: Beat-synced montage
looks.line: Music-led - cuts on the beat, speed changes into the drop, flashes and hits on the big moments.
looks.needs: A song and a run of moving shots: a trip, a place, a day out or an event. No talking needed.

looks.label: Cinematic travel
looks.line: A short film of a place - letterbox bars, slow motion, a filmic grade, place names in a corner, music and the place's own sound.

looks.label: Clean explainer
looks.line: Calm, clear teaching - chapter cards, labels that point at things, one idea at a time, music only between parts.

looks.label: Aesthetic day-in-the-life
looks.line: A calm diary of a day - soft warm colour, small lowercase notes and time stamps, the day's own sounds, gentle music.

looks.label: Documentary
looks.line: A short-film feel - a quiet cold open, date and place cards, serif titles, a muted grade, music that changes by scene.

looks.label: Faceless list
looks.line: A voice over b-roll working through a numbered list - big number cards, a progress counter, boxed captions.
looks.needs: A voiceover working through a short list, and clips of the things it names: hands, objects, places or screens. Missing shots come from stock or are made.

looks.label: High-energy challenge
looks.line: Retention-style - the goal and what is at stake in the first seconds, a running timer, attempts and setbacks, a re-hook every few seconds, a big result.

looks.label: Lots going on
looks.line: Maximum energy - a zoom, pop-up, sound or layout change every couple of seconds, and fast captions.

looks.label: Meme commentary
looks.line: Meme-format comedy - a caption bar over the clip, freeze frames, snap zooms with a boom, reaction emoji and sound stings, out on the punchline.

looks.label: Podcast episode
looks.line: A full video podcast or interview - the best moment as a cold open, the picture on whoever is talking, the wide shot to reset, names and chapters.

looks.label: Podcast clip, split screen
looks.line: Two people talking, stacked top and bottom, with captions on the seam in each speaker's colour.

looks.label: Product review
looks.line: A clean tech-style review - the product and one opinion up front, design to verdict in clear parts, spec cards, close detail shots, true colour.

looks.label: Storytime
looks.line: One person tells a story to camera - a title line that stays up, calm captions, slight zooms, a beat before the twist.
looks.needs: One person telling something that happened to them, to the camera, with clear speech and a turn or a payoff at the end.

looks.label: Travel vlog
looks.line: A story-led trip vlog - a cold open, day and place cards, talking parts between music-led montages, warm natural colour.

looks.label: Product ad (UGC)
looks.line: A creator-style product ad - the problem in the first seconds, the product in hand, proof points that tick in, the price, one clear ask.
looks.needs: One person showing a product they really use, in hand, with clear speech about what it does, what comes with it and what it costs.

looks.label: Word-pop talking head
looks.line: Big word-by-word captions, quick punch-ins and things popping up as they're said.
looks.needs: One person talking to the camera, close enough to punch in a little, with clear speech. Things they name can pop up as emoji, or their own pictures.

looks.label: Step by step
looks.line: How something is done or made: the result first, then each step with a big number and a few words.
looks.needs: Footage of something being done or made, start to finish: hands, tools and the material changing. Someone explaining as they go is welcome, not needed.

folders.label: Paper & craft
folders.line: Paper, prints and a pen, on one page.

folders.label: Pencil & ink
folders.line: Pencil, pen and wash on paper.
